findings.title: The work queues are unbounded, so slow processing provides no backpressure
findings.body: `queue.Queue()` is created without a `maxsize`, and `submit` uses a non-blocking-in-practice unbounded `put`. Therefore the Kafka strategy can continue polling and enqueueing indefinitely while one or more result processors are slow or unavailable. The stated natural backpressure never occurs; memory usage grows with the Kafka backlog and can OOM the consumer during a downstream outage. Use a bounded queue and make submission block or otherwise integrate its capacity with the processing strategy's backpressure mechanism.

findings.title: Processing failures are acknowledged and committed as successful
findings.body: The worker calls `complete_offset` in `finally`, including when `result_processor` raises. The exception is only logged, so the commit loop can advance the Kafka offset past a result that was not processed. This permanently drops the failed result instead of allowing Kafka retry/DLQ behavior, and contradicts the strategy's stated guarantee that offsets are committed only after successful processing. Only complete an offset after successful processing, with an explicit policy for failures.

findings.title: Queue shutdown uses APIs unavailable on supported pre-3.13 Python runtimes
findings.body: `Queue.shutdown()` and `queue.ShutDown` were introduced in Python 3.13. On earlier Python versions, `q.shutdown(...)` raises `AttributeError`, which is caught and logged, leaving workers blocked in `get`; each subsequent `join(timeout=5)` waits out its timeout. Normal consumer shutdown consequently leaks daemon worker threads and can stall shutdown for five seconds per queue. Use a sentinel-based shutdown or a compatibility mechanism unless the project runtime is explicitly Python 3.13+.

findings.title: The advertised graceful shutdown abandons queued work and stops commits before in-flight work finishes
findings.body: `shutdown` immediately sets every worker's `shutdown` flag, so each worker exits after at most its currently active item rather than draining its queue. In `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close`, the commit thread is stopped before this worker shutdown, so even an item that finishes during shutdown is not recorded as committed. A normal processor close can therefore abandon queued messages and replay already-processed in-flight messages after restart. Drain workers first (or explicitly terminate), then perform a final offset commit before stopping the commit loop.
